previous_statement: Upper norm bootstrap. For nonzero X, the target C*-lower axiom and node 1.3.2.1 give (1-epsilon)||gamma_n(X)||^2 <= ||gamma_n(X)^dagger gamma_n(X)|| <= (b_n+D e)||X||^2, because the source has ||X^dagger X||=||X||^2. Taking the supremum gives (1-epsilon)b_n^2<=b_n+D e. If b_n<=1 there is nothing to prove; otherwise, using epsilon<=e, b_n<=5, and e<=1, b_n(b_n-1)<=epsilon b_n^2+D e<=(25+D)e, hence b_n<=1+(25+D)e.
new_statement: Upper norm bootstrap in the common small-defect regime. Define e_bridge:=min{1,e_hom,e_mod} as in validated node 1.3.2.1, assume e:=rho+epsilon<e_bridge, and fix n. Let b_n:=sup_{X nonzero} ||gamma_n(X)||/||X||. Under this hypothesis node 1.3.2.1 supplies b_n<=5 and ||gamma_n(X^dagger X)-gamma_n(X)^dagger gamma_n(X)||<=D e||X||^2. Thus, for nonzero X, the target C*-lower axiom, the triangle inequality, and the exact source identity ||X^dagger X||=||X||^2 give (1-epsilon)||gamma_n(X)||^2<=||gamma_n(X)^dagger gamma_n(X)||<=(b_n+D e)||X||^2. Taking the supremum yields (1-epsilon)b_n^2<=b_n+D e, hence b_n(b_n-1)<=epsilon b_n^2+D e. If b_n<=1, then b_n<=1+(25+D)e because e>=0. If b_n>1, epsilon<=e and b_n<=5 give b_n(b_n-1)<=(25+D)e; division by b_n>=1 gives b_n<=1+(25+D)e. Therefore b_n<=1+(25+D)e for every n whenever e<e_bridge; no conclusion is asserted here outside that common small-defect regime.
